name: libass
listed_description: Portable subtitle renderer for the ASS/SSA subtitle format.
reason: No numbers against a baseline in README, Changelog (0.7 to 0.17.5), release notes or repo tree (checkasm, profile, compare, test dirs hold no published figures). Changelog says 'faster' for the 0.14.0 outline stroker (vs the FreeType stroker) and the 0.13.7 gaussian blur but gives no figures. Only external numbers found are a 2012 doom9 forum post (forum.doom9.org showthread p=1601006, host blocked here, snippet only, hardware unstated) with mplayer2 -benchmark -vo null: FATE ZERO OP1 libass 361 fps vs VSFilter 2.41.6205 + LAV Video 364 fps vs xy-VSFilter + LAV Video 552 fps, so libass is not faster there; the two search snippets disagree on other rows and the pipelines differ, so not usable. Lead: re-check that thread if doom9 becomes reachable.

name: libav
listed_description: A collection of libraries and tools to process multimedia content such as audio, video, subtitles and related metadata.
reason: No FFmpeg or other baseline comparison in README, Changelog, RELEASE (13_dev0), doc/RELEASE_NOTES or doc/faq.texi; Changelog 'faster H.264 decoding' and '35% faster VP3/Theora decoding' are version-to-version with no baseline. Repository is a mirror of git.libav.org with last commit 2019-04-16 (abandoned). Only outside numbers are anecdotal and unopenable here (hosts blocked, snippets only): a 2015 ffmpeg-devel patch email (2015-July/175115) mentions avconv 11.2 about 31 s vs ffmpeg 2.5.7 about 33 s on one 1080p H.264 file, and a reply says a -f rawvideo extra copy skews it; willus.com transcode benchmarks (2012, 2020) show Libav slower or mixed.

name: libavif
listed_description: Library for encoding and decoding .avif files.
reason: No benchmark in README, CHANGELOG.md (74 KB) or repo tree (no benchmark dir). Only speed statements: README says optional libyuv 'speeds up color space conversions' with no figures, and the 0.4.0 changelog says 'Split avifImageYUVToRGB into faster internal functions (estimated gain: 3.5x)', which is against its own earlier code and an estimate. AV1 encode and decode speed comes from the backends (libaom, dav1d, libgav1, rav1e, SVT-AV1); the libheif wiki AVIF Encoder Benchmark compares encoders through libheif, not libavif.

name: libcaca
reason: No benchmark or baseline comparison in README (no README.md; the plain README covers build only), NOTES or repo tree. Only speed statement is in NEWS: '30% speed increase in the bitmap rendering routine' for an old release, against its own earlier version with no setup. No comparison against aalib or any other renderer found.

name: libde265
reason: Numbers exist but none against another decoder. README: 284 fps 720p, 150 fps 1080p, 36 fps 4K via the GStreamer timehevc tool on i7-2700K, Ubuntu 12.04, GStreamer 0.10.36 (gstreamer-libde265 README has 298/161/40 fps for an older release). Wiki 'Decoder performance' (v0.7, i7-4960X, 1 to 12 thread table, for example ToS 4K(T) 28.82 fps at 1 thread to 125.11 fps at 12) is thread scaling only. Wiki 'Encoder comparison' is about encoders. No ffmpeg, OpenHEVC or HM row in README, wiki, libheif docs or issues. Lead: a KICS-IEEE paper 'Performance comparison of SIMD based HEVC decoders on mobile processors' (Galaxy S6) reportedly finds libde265 scales better than OpenHEVC with tile parallelism but is less efficient single-threaded (pure.skku.edu blocked here; mixed result, snippet only).

name: libharu
listed_description: A free, cross platform, open-sourced software library for generating PDF.
reason: Only speed claim is in README: 'A new-version library is about 4-15 times faster than a previous version' (libHaru 1.x C++ rewritten in C for 2.x), a self-comparison against an unnamed old version with no workload, hardware or methodology. No comparison against poppler, PDFium, PoDoFo or any other PDF library in README, CHANGES, issues (searched performance/faster/benchmark: only #357 and #95 appear) or a 2026 pistack.xyz blog survey (qualitative only).
